content: The metre per second (or meter per second in U.S. Speed is a scalar quantity, meaning it only has magnitude, while velocity is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and a specific direction. This unit is defined as the distance traveled in metres divided by the time taken in seconds. The official SI abbreviation for this unit is m·s⁻¹, which can also be written as m/s. Informally, the abbreviation mps is sometimes used. In cases where the metre per second is not a practical unit due to its relatively small scale, such as in astronomical contexts, velocities are often expressed in kilometres per second (km/s). One kilometre per second is equivalent to 1,000 metres per second. In non-scientific literature, the abbreviation kps is occasionally used instead of km/s. For reference, one metre per second is approximately the speed at which an average person walks. Conversions One metre per second is exactly equivalent to 1 foot per second multiplied by 0.3048 (1 ft/s = 0.3048 m·s⁻¹). One metre per second is approximately equivalent to 1 mile per hour multiplied by 0.4471 (1 mph ≈ 0.4471 m·s⁻¹). One metre per second is approximately equivalent to 1 kilometre per hour multiplied by 0.2778 (1 km/h ≈ 0.2778 m·s⁻¹). One kilometre per second is equivalent to 1,000 metres per second. Remark Although the metre per second is classified as an SI derived unit, it can be considered more fundamental than the metre itself. This is because the definition of the metre is based on the speed of light in a vacuum, which is defined as exactly 299,792,458 metres per second. Consequently, one metre is defined as the distance that light travels in a vacuum in 1/299,792,458 of a second.
